display_url_note: CDN URL - expires after few hours/days
combined_text:
Last month, Invest Newark CEO Marcus Randolph joined a panel hosted by the Newark Regional Business Partnership called the Regional Economic Outlook for 2026 -  Arts, Culture and the Economy. The discussion looked at how arts, entertainment, sports, and hospitality continue to shape growth in the Greater Newark region. Panelists talked about how these areas are boosting tourism, bringing in new investment, creating jobs, and opening more opportunities for local businesses.

description: A day honoring artist Aminah Robinson and reflecting on her life, legacy, and art. Enjoy a day filled with the ultimate kickback vibes. Get lost in art as we spend the day honoring artist Aminah Robinson and reflecting on her life and art that often revolved around the theme of home. Try making your own hogmawg, a clay-like mixture she made to create her sculptures, or enjoy a story reading of one of her books. Bask in the harmonies of vocalist @lyndastarrmusic & her band during a live jam session while journeying back to your youth with an option to partake in a Double Dutch performance by @floydsdoubledutchelite . It’s a day to celebrate community, artistic expression, and our newest special exhibition,Aminah Robinson: Journeys Home, A Visual Memoir.

Our strip woven textile from the Arts of Global Africa collection has traveled to the Brooklyn Museum! ✨ 

Strip weaving is a vibrant art form in West Africa. This stunning piece was created by the Bobo people, one of the largest ethnic groups in Burkina Faso. Weavers throughout the region use this traditional method—working on horizontal looms with foot pedals to craft long, narrow bands of cloth that are then sewn together to create wrappers, gowns, blankets, and more.

Our strip woven textile from the Arts of Global Africa collection has traveled to the Brooklyn Museum! ✨ 

Strip weaving is a vibrant art form in West Africa. This stunning piece was created by the Bobo people, one of the largest ethnic groups in Burkina Faso. Weavers throughout the region use this traditional method—working on horizontal looms with foot pedals to craft long, narrow bands of cloth that are then sewn together to create wrappers, gowns, blankets, and more. 

See it on view in Seyd
